chunks: 191 - Al-Ḥalabī said: And one who heard him narrated to me that he was saying:
If the junub immerses himself in the water in a single immersion, that suffices him for his ghusl.

Whoever becomes junub during a day or a night multiple times, one ghusl suffices him, unless he becomes junub after the ghusl or has a wet dream. If he has a wet dream, then he should not have intercourse until he performs ghusl from the wet dream.

There is no harm in the junub reciting the whole Qur'an except the passages of obligation of prostration in which one prostrates, and they are the sajdah of Luqmān, Ḥā-Mīm al-Sajdah, al-Najm, and Sūrat Iqraʾ bi-smi Rabbika. Whoever is junub or without wudu should not touch the Qur'an, though it is permissible for him to touch the paper or for another person to turn the pages for him, while he reads and remembers Allah, Mighty and Majestic.

It is not permissible for the menstruating woman and the junub to enter the mosque except while passing through, and they may take something from it, but they may not place anything in it, because what is in it they cannot take from elsewhere, while they are able to place what is with them elsewhere.

If a woman intends to perform ghusl from janabah and menstruation comes upon her, then she should leave the ghusl until she becomes pure. When she becomes pure, she performs one ghusl for janabah and menstruation.

There is no harm in the junub applying dye, becoming junub while dyed, undergoing cupping, remembering Allah, Exalted is He, using depilatory treatment, slaughtering, wearing a ring, sleeping in the mosque and passing through it, or becoming junub at the beginning of the night and sleeping until its end. Whoever becomes junub in a land and finds no water except frozen water and cannot reach the earth, then let him pray with wiping, then let him not return to the land in which he imperils his religion.

And my father, may Allah have mercy on him, said in his epistle to me: There is no harm in dividing the ghusl. You wash your hands, your private part, and your head, and delay washing your body until the time of salat, then wash your body when you wish to do so. If you incur a state of hadath from urination, defecation, or wind after washing your head and before washing your body, then repeat the ghusl from its beginning. If you begin with washing your body before the head, then repeat the ghusl over your body after washing your head.

key_terms.الصَّعِيدِ: earth or clean ground relevant to dry purification when water is inaccessible
key_terms.الْجُنُبُ: a person in the state of janabah, requiring ghusl
key_terms.الْحَيْضِ: menstruation, which can be combined with janabah in one ghusl
key_terms.الْقُرْآنَ: the Qur'an, whose recitation and touching are discussed here
key_terms.الْمَسْجِدَ: the mosque, whose entry has rulings for the junub and menstruating woman
key_terms.غُسْلِهِ: his ritual bath for removing janabah
key_terms.وُضُوءٍ: wudu, the state of ritual ablution

ai.seo_question: What are the rulings on ghusl, Qur'an recitation, and mosque entry for a person in janabah?
ai.summary: This hadith gathers several legal rulings related to janabah, including how ghusl suffices, repeated janabah, recitation and touching of the Qur'an, mosque entry, and combined ghusl for janabah and menstruation. It also addresses practical cases such as tayammum-like wiping when water is inaccessible and the permissibility of certain actions while junub, concluding with instructions on the proper sequence of ghusl.
